answers.answer: The draw deck is the 12 Speed cards, 3 Starting Upgrade cards, and 3 Stress cards shuffled together. Put the 6 Heat cards face up on the Engine spot, set the Gear pawn to 1st, and draw 7 cards.
answers.evidence: Setup: steps 4–6 and 9.

answers.answer: You may stay in the same gear. You may shift two positions (such as 1st to 3rd) by paying 1 Heat immediately during Shift Gears, moving it from your Engine to your discard pile; you must have that Heat available then.
answers.evidence: Simultaneous Phase, step 1: 'Stay in your current gear' and a two-position shift costs 1 Heat during this step, moved from Engine to discard.

answers.answer: No. In 3rd gear you must play 3 cards. Play them face down.
answers.evidence: Simultaneous Phase, step 2: play cards face down equal to your gear number.

answers.answer: Steps 1 and 2 are simultaneous for all players, in that order. Everyone finishes both before step 3 begins. In the sequential phase, each player completes steps 3–9 before the next player starts; the frontmost car acts first, and for side-by-side cars the one closest to the Race Line is ahead and acts first.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Sequential Phase: all players complete steps 1–2 simultaneously; then each player completes steps 3–9 front car first; Race Line resolves side-by-side order.

answers.answer: Cars do not block passage. If the destination space is full, put your car in the first free spot behind the blocking cars. When placing your car, use the spot closest to the Race Line if it is available.
answers.evidence: Reveal & Move: place on the spot closest to Race Line if available. Blocked Movement: cars never block passage; a full destination places you in the first free spot behind blockers.

answers.answer: Discard the flipped Heat card and Starting Upgrade card immediately because they are non-Speed cards. Put the revealed Speed 3 on top of the played Stress card in the Play Area; it supplies speed 3, and both the found Speed and played Stress are discarded during Replenish Hand. Resolve Stress before Adrenaline.
answers.evidence: Stress Cards: discard each flipped non-Speed card; put the found Speed card on top of the played Stress and discard both during Replenish Hand. Step 3 says finish Stress before Adrenaline.

answers.answer: In a five-car race, the last two cars to move get Adrenaline. Each may use an extra Cooldown and add 1 extra speed, either benefit, both, or neither. The extra speed may be taken before or after Boost. Unused Adrenaline cannot be saved for another round.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: if race started with 5 or more cars, the last two receive benefits; either/both/neither; extra speed before or after Boost; unused benefit cannot be saved.

answers.answer: Yes. In 2nd gear you have Cooldown 1, so during React you may return one Heat from hand to Engine. You may then spend it immediately to Boost, paying it from Engine to discard. The summary permits Cooldown and Boost symbols in any order and says cooled Heat may be spent immediately.
answers.evidence: React: 'You may Cooldown Heat from your hand into your Engine, then immediately spend it to Boost.' Cooldown lists 2nd gear allowance 1; Paying Heat and Boost describe payment from Engine.

answers.answer: You may Boost once per turn during React, paying 1 Heat from your Engine to discard. If the Engine is empty, you cannot choose to Boost unless you first Cooldown Heat from hand into the Engine during React. Flip cards until a Speed card appears, immediately discarding each non-Speed; add and move by that Speed card's value. Boost speed counts for corner checks.
answers.evidence: Boost; Paying Heat; React; Check Corner: Boost is once per turn, costs 1 Engine Heat, uses the flip-until-Speed procedure, and counts toward total speed for corner checks.

answers.answer: Slipstream is optional. Check speed 6, excluding Slipstream movement; since 6 exceeds the limit 4 by 2, pay 2 Heat.
answers.evidence: Slipstream is optional; Check Corner says use total speed including Boost/Adrenaline but excluding Slipstream, and pay Heat equal to the excess over each limit.

answers.answer: Check both corners in the order crossed. Pay 2 Heat for the limit-6 corner and 4 for the limit-4 corner, 6 Heat altogether.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: check every crossed Corner Line in order, separately, using the same total speed; pay excess over each limit.

answers.answer: You cannot pay the 3 Heat required with only 2 available, so you spin out and move all remaining Engine Heat to your discard pile. Return to the first available space before that corner. Take 2 extra Stress cards directly into your hand because you were in 4th gear, then set your gear to 1st.
answers.evidence: Spin Out: if unable to pay enough, move all remaining Engine Heat to discard, move back before the corner, take 2 Stress into hand in 3rd/4th gear, then move to 1st.

answers.answer: You may discard unwanted Speed cards, but not Stress or Heat cards. You may not browse any discard pile, including your own; only the top card of each pile is public knowledge.
answers.evidence: Discard step: may discard unwanted cards but never Stress or Heat; nobody may browse any discard pile; only each pile's top card is public.

answers.answer: Move all Play Area cards to your discard pile, then draw only enough to bring your hand back to 7, not seven additional cards.
answers.evidence: Replenish Hand, step 9.

answers.answer: Shuffle your discard pile into a new draw deck immediately, then continue the interrupted Stress flips. Do not include cards still in your Play Area; they have not yet been discarded.
answers.evidence: Running Out of Cards: shuffle discard into a new draw deck and continue interrupted draws/flips; do not include Play Area cards.

answers.answer: When paid, Heat moves from Engine to discard. It can cycle from discard to draw deck to hand, then return to Engine only via Cooldown. Heat cannot normally be played or voluntarily discarded from hand.
answers.evidence: Paying Heat; Heat Card Cycle; final Special Rules bullet.

answers.answer: Commit the 2 playable cards and fill the remaining 2 required slots with Heat cards in the Play Area. Move zero spaces, set gear to 1st, discard all committed cards including the covering Heat, and skip directly to step 9. You skip React, so cannot Cooldown or Boost this turn.
answers.evidence: Cluttered Hand: commit playable cards and fill slots with Heat; move zero; set gear to 1st; discard all committed cards; skip directly to step 9 and React.

answers.answer: No, crossing first in the round does not automatically win. If multiple cars finish in the same round, the car furthest ahead wins, with the Race Line position breaking a tie. At the end of the round, remove all cars that crossed the final finish line and place them in finishing order on the Hall of Fame.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: same-round finishers are ordered by furthest ahead (Race Line breaks ties); at round end remove finishers to Hall of Fame.

answers.answer: No. On the final lap, you cannot Slipstream across the finish line or Slipstream after crossing it. After crossing the final finish line, ignore speed limits of corners beyond it and move as far as you can.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions and Slipstream / Check Corner: final-lap Slipstream restrictions and exemption from later corner limits.

answers.answer: Both remaining cars receive Adrenaline, because the race started with six cars. Eligibility uses the number that started the race even after finishers leave; with 5 or more starters, the last two cars to move get it.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: use number of cars that started, even after finishers leave; 5 or more starters means last two.

answers.answer: Use the number of laps printed on the selected board. USA normally uses 2 laps; for a first USA learning race, the summary suggests racing just 1 lap instead.
answers.evidence: Setup step 1: use laps printed on selected board; first USA learning race may be 1 lap instead of its normal 2.

answers.answer: No. Check the board for how many Heat and Stress cards each player adds; the summary says it is typically 6 Heat and 3 Stress, rather than stating that every track always uses those numbers.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3.

answers.answer: Randomly assign participating cars to the starting grid, placing them one at a time and filling numbered spots in ascending order. This establishes first-round order; players do not choose preferred positions.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Place the remaining Stress cards face up near the board as a reserve.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: The optional handicap is for the experienced driver to remove 1 or 2 Heat from their own car.
answers.evidence: Optional handicap in Setup.

answers.answer: No. The largest shift is two positions in one step, and it costs 1 Heat; shifting three positions from 1st to 4th is not allowed by the described options.
answers.evidence: Shift Gears: stay, shift up/down one for free, or shift two by paying 1 Heat; Player Reference repeats the two-position examples.

answers.answer: No. The two-position shift must be paid immediately during Shift Gears from Heat available in the Engine. Heat in hand cannot pay, and React Cooldown occurs later.
answers.evidence: Shift Gears step 1 requires immediately paying Engine Heat during that step; Paying Heat says hand Heat cannot pay.

answers.answer: Each played Stress card gets its own flip-until-Speed resolution. The two found Speed cards provide 3 and 4, in addition to the played Speed 2, for total speed 9. They are added to the Play Area by resolving Stress; they are not extra cards committed from hand.
answers.evidence: Stress Cards: 'For each Stress card' flip until a Speed appears; found Speed supplies that Stress card's speed and is put in Play Area on top of it. Step 2 sets committed hand cards equal to gear.

answers.answer: No. You must move forward exactly the total speed; you cannot voluntarily stop short to avoid a corner.
answers.evidence: Reveal & Move, step 3.

answers.answer: Use speed 8, not the 5 spaces actually moved. The full destination causing shorter movement does not change the speed used for corner checks; at limit 6, pay 2 Heat if able.
answers.evidence: Reveal & Move describes blocked movement; Check Corner compares total speed for the round with the limit and pays the excess.

answers.answer: No. A corner check is triggered by crossing a Corner Line; being near it without crossing does not require payment.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: check every Corner Line crossed; if no line is crossed, no check is indicated.

answers.answer: No Heat is due at speed 6 or below for a limit-6 corner, so an empty Engine does not cause payment or a spin out by itself. Payment is only the excess over the limit; spin out is described when you cannot pay Heat required for a corner.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: if speed does not exceed limit, pay nothing. Spin Out only applies if you cannot pay enough Heat for a corner.

answers.answer: You successfully pay all 3 Heat and continue. The summary says spin out occurs if you cannot pay enough; it does not require Heat to remain after paying.
answers.evidence: Spin Out: 'If you cannot pay enough Heat for a corner' then spin out; Paying Heat moves the required cards from Engine to discard.

answers.answer: The first corner costs 2 Heat (8−6), leaving 3. The second costs 4 (8−4), which you cannot fully pay, so the limit-4 corner causes the spin out. Move all remaining Engine Heat to discard, return to the first available space before that corner, take 2 Stress directly into hand for 4th gear, and end in 1st gear.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: check corners separately in order using same speed. Spin Out: insufficient payment sends remaining Engine Heat to discard, returns car before the corner that caused spin out, takes Stress into hand based on gear, then sets 1st.

answers.answer: Take 1 extra Stress card directly into your hand for 2nd gear, then set your Gear pawn to 1st.
answers.evidence: Spin Out: 1 Stress in 1st/2nd gear is taken directly into hand; then move Gear pawn to 1st.

answers.answer: 1st gear provides Cooldown 3. Adrenaline adds 1, for a maximum of 4 Heat cooled from hand into Engine. You may cool fewer cards or none; you are not forced to use the full allowance.
answers.evidence: Player Reference: 1st gear Cooldown 3. Cooldown: fewer or none allowed; Adrenaline adds 1 to allowance.

answers.answer: Yes. You may decline the extra speed while still using the extra Cooldown; each benefit may be used, both, or neither.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: may use either benefit, both, or neither; declining extra speed does not prevent extra Cooldown.

answers.answer: Yes. Adrenaline goes to the last car(s) to move, so you remain eligible even if your move ends in the lead. In a four-car race, only the last car receives it; the second-to-last does not.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: last car to move gets benefits; only when race started with 5 or more cars do the last two get them.

answers.answer: You qualify if you end next to another car or in the space immediately behind a car. If neither applies, you do not qualify.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: if you end next to another car or in the space immediately behind a car, optionally move 2 spaces.

answers.answer: Yes. Slipstream eligibility is assessed at the Slipstream step, after React; if Boost then leaves you immediately behind a car, you meet the stated end-position condition.
answers.evidence: Turn order places React (step 5) before Slipstream (step 6), which qualifies based on whether you end next to or immediately behind a car.

answers.answer: Just one two-space Slipstream move. Qualifying next to or behind multiple cars does not multiply the move.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: qualifying next to or behind multiple cars does not multiply this move.

answers.answer: Slipstream does not permit sharing an occupied spot. Apply normal Blocked Movement placement: if the destination is full, place the car in the first free spot behind the blocking cars. Reduced movement does not change the speed used for corner checks; Slipstream movement is excluded from check speed.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: full landing uses normal Blocked Movement; no sharing; shorter movement does not change corner-check speed. Blocked Movement gives first free spot behind blockers.

answers.answer: No. The pre-finish limit-4 corner is checked and costs 4 Heat at speed 8. The corner beyond the final finish line is ignored, so total Heat due is 4.
answers.evidence: Scoring: after crossing final finish line, ignore speed limits of corners beyond it. Check Corner otherwise charges speed excess for each crossed corner.

answers.answer: Yes, an otherwise legal Slipstream on an intermediate lap may cross the start/finish line, and corners beyond it still have their normal speed limits.
answers.evidence: Scoring: on intermediate laps legal Slipstream may cross start/finish; normal corner limits still apply beyond it.

answers.answer: The other cars continue racing. At the end of the round remove all cars that crossed the final finish line; continue until all cars finish.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: remove finishers at end of round and continue playing until all cars finish.

answers.answer: No. In the core game, crossing a Corner Line triggers a corner check; the Legends Line is used only in advanced play and crossing it alone does not trigger core-game corner payment.
answers.evidence: Track Lines: Corner Line triggers a check in core game; Legends Line is only for advanced play and alone is not a core-game payment trigger.

answers.answer: No. Shift Gears happens before Play Cards, so after shifting from 3rd to 2nd you must commit 2 cards. With two playable cards, you meet that requirement and do not have Cluttered Hand.
answers.evidence: Simultaneous Phase: step 1 Shift Gears precedes step 2 Play Cards; play cards equal to gear number. Cluttered Hand applies when too few playable cards for your gear.
